headline: ASX closes up 0.46% to break 9,000 as gold surges to record $4,473/oz on US-Iran war fears — your portfolio is broadly green today.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped last night despite big news: the company announced it will start separately disclosing Azure cloud revenue for the first time, restructuring its reporting. Markets may be digesting what this transparency reveals about growth rates. Down slightly but nothing structural has changed — the long-term cloud and AI story remains intact.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: A solid day for VDHG, riding the broader ASX 200 gain of 0.46% and buoyed by positive global market sentiment. No single catalyst — just a good broad market session.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets ticked higher today, helped by a slightly stronger AUD and calmer global risk sentiment. The Aussie dollar rising to 71.7 US cents is a mild headwind for this AUD-denominated ETF's returns when you look through to the underlying, but the price still moved up.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google edged higher last night, helped by enthusiasm around its new Gemini 3.8 Flash model launch — performance benchmarks are reportedly close to top rival Claude Opus 5. Positive AI newsflow is giving Alphabet a lift.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS gained today, tracking last night's solid S&P 500 and NASDAQ performance. Broad US market strength flowed through to this ETF's ASX price.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up slightly today. NVIDIA's blockbuster Q2 revenue of $96 billion is a positive signal for AI chip demand, which underpins many of this ETF's holdings. Still underwater on total investment, but the AI thematic remains strong.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS edged barely higher today — a flat session for lithium stocks broadly. Pilbara remains in focus among lithium investors but the sector is still waiting for a meaningful catalyst to lift prices off depressed levels.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two dipped a fraction last night — no specific news catalyst. Still the portfolio's biggest loss-maker in dollar terms. The long-term story here is GTA VI, which hasn't changed.

watch_today.title: Gold hits record $4,473/oz — tailwind for the broader market
watch_today.detail: Gold surged 2.44% last night to a record $4,473 USD per ounce, driven by rising geopolitical fear as US-Iran military exchanges continue. This tends to support defensive assets and can weigh on risk appetite for equities — worth watching if the conflict escalates further this week.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike looms — hold VDHG and VTS, stay the course
watch_today.detail: Multiple outlets today (AFR, News.com.au) are reporting the RBA now has the economic data it needs to lift interest rates this month. Australia's GDP growth data has come in stronger than expected, which paradoxically makes a rate hike more likely. Higher rates can weigh on ASX growth stocks short-term. For a long-term holder of diversified ETFs like VDHG and VTS, this is noise — sit tight.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Azure transparency is a positive long-term signal — hold
watch_today.detail: Microsoft announced last night it will begin breaking out Azure cloud revenue as a separate line item in its earnings — a first. This is a significant structural change: it either confirms Azure's strength or exposes slower growth. Either way, it's more transparency, which is generally good for long-term investors. Last night's -0.84% dip is not a concern. Hold.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI newsflow strong, but still down 14% overall — hold
watch_today.detail: NVIDIA's Q2 FY27 revenue hit a staggering $96 billion (way above expectations), Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash, and OpenAI released new cyber-capable models. The AI thematic underpinning GXAI is firing on all cylinders. The ETF is up 0.19% today and the sector tailwinds are real — but you're sitting on a -14.3% loss overall. No reason to sell; the long-term AI story is intact. Hold and let it run.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium still searching for a floor — hold for now
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals ticked up marginally today but remains down 22.85% on your total investment. There's no new catalyst to move lithium prices meaningfully higher right now. For a long-term holder, the thesis depends on EV demand recovery — that story is intact but patience is required. No reason to sell at these levels.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA VI thesis unchanged — hold
watch_today.detail: Take-Two slipped a tiny 0.25% last night with no news. You're down 6.9% overall. The entire investment case for TTWO is the eventual GTA VI release cycle — nothing has changed that story. A long-term hold is the right call here; don't let small daily moves spook you.

world.summary: The dominant global story is the continuing US-Iran military conflict, which is rattling energy markets and pushing gold to record highs. Canada-US trade tensions are also simmering, while the rest of the world watches gold surge past $4,400.

stories.title: US and Iran Trade Military Strikes in New Flare-Up
stories.why_it_matters: The US and Iran have exchanged fresh military strikes, reigniting fears of a broader Middle East war. Trump has said the US is prepared to resume strikes on Iran 'at any time', while the Pentagon has extended its Middle East military deployments into 2027. This conflict is the main reason gold has surged to record highs above $4,400/oz — investors are piling into safe-haven assets. Oil remains elevated near $90/barrel. For everyday Australians, this could mean higher petrol prices and increased market volatility if the conflict escalates further.

stories.title: Pentagon Extends Middle East Deployments Into 2027
stories.why_it_matters: The US military has formally extended its deployments across the Middle East through to 2027, signalling Washington sees no quick end to the Iran conflict. This is a significant escalation in commitment — more US troops and assets in the region for the long haul. The ripple effects include sustained pressure on oil supplies, ongoing risk of shipping disruption through the Strait of Hormuz (a key chokepoint for global energy), and continued upward pressure on defence spending globally.

stories.title: Canada's PM Carney Tells Trump Officials to 'Stop Throwing Shade' Over Trade Talks
stories.why_it_matters: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has publicly told Trump administration officials to stop undermining Canada-US trade negotiations — blunt language from a close US ally. Trade talks between the two countries are continuing but are clearly tense. Canada is Australia's fellow middle-power ally and a major commodity exporter; a fractured Canada-US relationship creates ripple effects across global trade norms and could affect how other nations (including Australia) negotiate with Washington.

stories.title: Gold Surges 2.4% to Record $4,473/oz as War Fears Mount
stories.why_it_matters: Gold smashed through to a new record high last night, jumping over $106 to close at $4,473 USD per ounce — a 2.44% single-session move. The primary driver is safe-haven buying as the US-Iran conflict intensifies and investors seek protection. This is significant for Australian investors: a rising gold price is generally good news for ASX-listed gold miners, and it reflects genuine global anxiety about geopolitical stability. If you hold gold miners or gold ETFs (not currently in this portfolio), they'd be surging.

stories.title: Vietnam's Mobile Internet Speed Breaks Into Global Top 10, Ahead of US and China
stories.why_it_matters: Vietnam has ranked inside the global top 10 for mobile internet speed, overtaking both the US and China — a remarkable achievement for an emerging economy. This reflects massive infrastructure investment across Southeast Asia and signals Vietnam's growing digital economy competitiveness. For investors in emerging markets ETFs like VGE, Southeast Asian growth stories like this are part of the broader emerging markets tailwind.

markets.summary: The ASX closed up a solid 0.46% to 9,020 — staying comfortably above the 9,000 level. Last night, US markets were also positive: the S&P 500 gained 0.46% and the NASDAQ rose 0.45%. The big story in commodities is gold rocketing to a record $4,473/oz. Oil dipped slightly to $90.51. The Aussie dollar nudged up to 71.7 US cents.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Last night's session — tech broadly positive.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Record high — US-Iran war fears driving safe-haven buying.

indicators.note: Slight dip but remains elevated near $90.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is the RBA and whether it will hike interest rates this month. Australia's stronger-than-expected economic growth has given the central bank the green light — but it's a double-edged sword for households.

stories.title: RBA Now Has the Data It Needs to Hike Rates This Month — AFR
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR is reporting that Australia's latest economic data — including stronger-than-expected GDP growth — has given the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) the evidence it needs to lift the official cash rate at its September meeting. A rate hike means higher mortgage repayments for anyone with a variable-rate home loan. It also tends to slow down the share market as borrowing costs rise across the economy. The RBA is caught between fighting inflation and not crushing growth.

stories.title: Australia's Stronger Growth Has a Sting in the Tail
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's economy grew faster than expected, which sounds like great news — but the cost is that it gives the RBA more reason to keep interest rates higher for longer. The 'growth rut' narrative that had been building (giving hope for rate cuts) is now less convincing. Households that were hoping for mortgage relief may have to wait longer. Higher rates also push up the value of the Australian dollar, which affects exporters and overseas investors.

stories.title: Rising Government Debt Is Spooking the Bond Market
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's government debt is rising, and bond market investors — the people who lend money to governments — are getting nervous. When bond investors get worried, they demand higher interest rates to compensate for the risk, which pushes up borrowing costs across the whole economy (mortgages, business loans, credit cards). The Conversation explains that this debt anxiety is a structural issue, not just a short-term blip, and could constrain future government spending on things like healthcare and infrastructure.

ai.summary: A massive week for AI news: Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash, OpenAI unveiled its first model with 'critical' cyber capabilities, and a global debate is intensifying over how (or whether) to regulate AI — with the US pushing for a hands-off approach and the EU going the other direction.

stories.title: Google Launches Gemini 3.8 Flash — Rivals Top Models at a Fraction of the Cost
stories.why_it_matters: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash, a new AI model that reportedly performs close to the benchmark-topping Claude Opus 5 — but at much lower cost. This matters because it keeps Google highly competitive in the AI race against Anthropic and OpenAI. For GOOG holders, continued AI product momentum is exactly what you want to see. The model is also specifically designed for 'vibe coding' (AI-assisted programming), signalling Google is targeting developers as a key market.

stories.title: OpenAI Releases First AI Model With 'Critical' Cyber Capabilities
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has released what it's calling 'Astra' — its first AI model with 'critical' cyber security capabilities. WIRED reports this means the model can perform tasks in cybersecurity that were previously only possible for expert human hackers. This raises both exciting possibilities (automated defence, vulnerability scanning) and serious safety concerns (could it help bad actors?). Google and Anthropic have simultaneously released their own cyber AI models and safeguards, signalling the whole industry is moving into this sensitive territory at once.

stories.title: US Pushes Light-Touch AI Rules at G20; EU Goes the Other Way
stories.why_it_matters: At this week's G20 tech meeting, the US struck a 'light-touch' AI regulation deal with member nations — basically agreeing not to impose heavy rules on AI development. The EU is moving in the opposite direction with stricter laws. For AI companies like Google and Microsoft, a looser US regulatory environment is good news — less compliance cost and more freedom to ship products. Australia sits somewhere in the middle and will likely need to choose a lane soon.

stories.title: US States Are Defying Washington and Tech Lobby on AI Rules
stories.why_it_matters: Even as the federal US government pushes for minimal AI regulation, individual US states are moving to regulate AI anyway — driven by voter concern about deepfakes, job losses, and AI-generated misinformation. This creates a complicated patchwork of rules that tech companies have to navigate. It could add friction and compliance costs for companies like Google and Microsoft operating across multiple states, even if federal rules stay light.

sport.summary: NRL Round 27 is underway — Bulldogs vs Broncos kicks off tonight at Accor Stadium. In AFL, the Sydney Swans scandal is narrowing, and Fremantle faces a double injury hurdle heading into finals.

stories.title: Sydney Swans Scandal Narrows to Four Players — Police Update
stories.why_it_matters: Police investigating the alleged sexual assault scandal involving Sydney Swans players have confirmed they are 'not looking for anyone further' — narrowing the focus to four players. 7NEWS reports this is a significant update that tightens the investigation's scope. The AFL club is in the middle of its finals campaign, making this one of the most distracting and damaging scandals in recent AFL history.

stories.title: AFL Scores Record 370 Million Global Audience
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL has announced a record global audience of 370 million fans tuned in this season — a remarkable number that underlines the code's growing international footprint. This is significant for sponsors and broadcasters, and strengthens the AFL's negotiating position for future broadcast rights deals. For Gold Coast Suns fans, a bigger global pie is good news for the game's long-term health.

stories.title: Fremantle's Double Injury Headache Ahead of AFL Finals
stories.why_it_matters: Fremantle is facing a double injury concern heading into the AFL finals — Fox Sports reports the club has a 'double hurdle' threatening their premiership run. With the 'Fraser v Ali' matchup being closely watched as a key individual contest, any fitness doubts could significantly alter how Fremantle approaches their finals campaign.

stories.title: NRL Round 27 Kicks Off Tonight: Bulldogs vs Broncos at Accor Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: Round 27 is underway — the Bulldogs host the Broncos tonight at 7:50pm at Accor Stadium. With the finals just around the corner, this is a crucial match for both clubs' finishing positions. Local Gold Coast fans have the Titans vs Dolphins on Friday night at 6pm at Cbus Super Stadium — a local derby to keep an eye on.

stories.title: Warriors Release Experienced Back; Dragons Prodigy Attracting Big-Money Interest
stories.why_it_matters: The Warriors have told an experienced back he is free to find another club ahead of next season, while a Dragons youngster is being circled by a rival club with serious money to spend. Heading into the final rounds of the regular season, player movement news is picking up as clubs jockey for position ahead of the off-season transfer window.
